title: Cloud Resource Count Trending

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.6.1 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.6.1 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`aws:config:notification` collected via Splunk Add-on for AWS, Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services, Google Cloud add-ons; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: Splunk Add-on for AWS, Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services, Google Cloud add-ons
spl:
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:config:notification" resourceType="AWS::EC2::Instance"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.6.1_cloud_resource_count_tre_1"
| sort -_time
description: EC2/VM instance count over 90 days reveals organic growth, failed automation leaving orphan instances, or shrinkage after optimization campaigns. Supports FinOps conversations and capacity forecasts.
value: Detecting cloud resource count trending early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Ingest periodic inventory snapshots (AWS Config, DescribeInstances exports, or Azure Resource Graph) into index=cloud with one event per instance per snapshot. If only change streams exist, maintain state with a nightly summary search. Chart instance_count over 90 days; optionally split by accountId or region. For multi-cloud, normalize resourceType across providers.
visualization: Line chart (instance count over 90 days with trend and 30-day forecast), area chart stacked by account.

references.title: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services

knownFalsePositives: Inventories can skip a run when an API is throttled or a connector is in maintenance, which looks like a big drop. We check the ingest time and the last good snapshot before we call it shrinkage.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure Splunk Add-on for AWS, Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services, Google Cloud add-ons with the modular input for `aws:config:notification`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.6.7.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest periodic inventory snapshots (AWS Config, DescribeInstances exports, or Azure Resource Graph) into index=cloud with one event per instance per snapshot. If only change streams exist, maintain state with a nightly summary search. Chart instance_count over 90 days; optionally split by accountId or region. For multi-cloud, normalize resourceType across providers.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:config:notification" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="aws:config:notification" resourceType="AWS::EC2::Instance"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.6.1_cloud_resource_count_tre_1"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:config:notification` in `index=cloud` to detect cloud resource count trending. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_6_1_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (instance count over 90 days with trend and 30-day forecast), area chart stacked by account..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Add-on for AWS, Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services, Google Cloud add-ons and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloud resource count trending so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
